name: Inema Arts Center
funding: Artist-run centre founded in 2012 by painter brothers Innocent Nkurunziza and Emmanuel Nkuranga.
watch: Ten resident-artist slots at KG 563 St, Kacyiru. A funder list is not published.
records_note: Inema's site names its two founders but no funders, reports, accounts or board; a Support Inema page exists but was not readable.

name: The Muse Multi Studios
funding: Won Culture Resource's Abbara Program grant (round 7, 2022). The Australian Government and Creative Australia support its Qubit fellowship (2026). The Spanish Embassy is a named partner.
watch: Opened Muse Gallery in Khartoum in 2022; since the April 2023 war it works between Sudan and Egypt and runs the Sudan Art Archive.
records_note: Posts narrative year reviews for 2023 to 2025 with no figures; no accounts, no standing funder list, and only its five staff are named.

name: Institute of Contemporary Art Indian Ocean (ICAIO)
funding: Founded in 2015 by Salim Currimjee, a painter, architect and collector.
watch: Exhibitions change each quarter, showing Mauritian, Indian and South African artists, at 51 Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Street, Port Louis.
records_note: icaio.org now redirects to an unrelated gambling site, so ICAIO's own pages could not be read.

name: Nhaka Gallery (formerly Gallery Delta)
funding: Operates under the Women's Gallery Arts and Research Trust. Its March 2023 show had support from the Swiss and Australian embassies and UN Women. No funder list is published.
watch: Gallery Delta was founded in 1975 by Derek Huggins and Helen Lieros, who died in 2021; Nhaka presents itself as continuing that legacy.
records_note: No Nhaka Gallery website was found; the only named backers are for one 2023 show, and no reports, accounts or board appear.

name: Lusaka Contemporary Art Centre (LuCAC)
funding: Founder Victor Mutelekesha's household paid for the building. Pro Helvetia paid for shelving; OCA, a Norwegian arts body, part-financed the 2023 opening show; the late artist Jan Groth donated.
watch: Opened 6 January 2023 in New Chamba Valley with a gallery, library and artist residency; first show Prospice, Kwacha!
records_note: Names its eleven-member advisory board; publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list.

name: Associação Núcleo de Arte
funding: Artists' association with over 100 members. State funding ended in the civil war; a late-1990s profile names Hivos as donor. No current funder list is published.
watch: Official foundation 1948; reopened in 1993 by young artists. Maputo's council and the CTA led a 2021 mural project with 40 of its members.
records_note: The association's only page found is a late-1990s profile naming Hivos; it publishes no reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Nesr Art Foundation
funding: Funded by Wissam and Hiba Nesr. Wissam is chief executive of Webcor Group, a Swiss-based food importer and distributor with most African revenue in Angola. No outside funders named.
watch: Opened in 2021 with a residency for Angolan and Lusophone African artists; the artistic committee is chaired by Paula Nascimento.
records_note: Names its eight-member advisory board and three-member artistic committee; publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list, being paid for by its founders.

name: Franco-Namibian Cultural Centre (FNCC)
funding: Binational centre under Namibian law, funded by the French government. Namibia gave the land and France paid for the building; foundation stone laid in 1998.
watch: Has a large multipurpose gallery and hosts exhibitions at 118 Robert Mugabe Avenue, Windhoek.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports, accounts or funder list; its Team page names the director and staff but no board.

name: Botswana National Museum and Art Gallery
funding: Statutory museum set up by Act of Parliament in 1967 and run by the Department of National Museum and Monuments. Government funded its P33 million refurbishment, begun in 2020.
watch: Includes the National Art Gallery and the Octagon Gallery. Opened to the public in 1968.
records_note: Its official site is down and no ministry report could be opened, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara (MuCAT)
funding: Built on the initiative of Adama Toungara, then mayor of Abobo; the director says it was built from own funds.
watch: Stands opposite Abobo town hall on 3,500 m², designed by architect Issa Diabaté. Opened with the pan-African show Prête-moi ton rêve.
records_note: MuCAT's site lists a team but no board, partners, reports or accounts; it says the museum is private, foundation-owned and gets no state subsidy.

name: Festival International des Arts du Bénin (FInAB)
funding: Run by Groupe Empire's events arm with Benin government support through its arts fund (FDAC). MTN partnered the 2026 edition, Canal+ Impact 2025. Other partners unnamed; no budget published.
watch: Festival in Cotonou, Porto-Novo and Ouidah. The fourth edition closed in early March 2026, with days for Nigeria, Togo, Lebanon and Morocco.
records_note: No FInAB website was found; press names organiser Groupe Empire, the culture ministry and different sponsors each year, with no reports, accounts or board.

name: Dar Foto Festival
funding: Founded by Andrew Munuwa with Valentin Rudloff.
watch: Launched in 2023. The 2025 edition showed 15 artists from Congo, Sudan, Kenya and Tanzania in Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar.
records_note: The festival's site darfotofestival.com did not resolve, so nothing was checked; a fundraising page shows individual donors only.
